[attribute-source-id]
=== `@source-id` Source Identifier (in Related Object)

Identifier of a journal, book, conference proceedings, or other publication that is (or contains) the target of the <<element-related-object,`<related-object>`>>.

#### Usage/Remarks
Used along with <<attribute-source-id-type,`@source-id-type`>> to identify the publication that is (or contains) the target of the <<element-related-object,`<related-object>`>> element. The <<attribute-source-id,`@source-id`>> might contain an ISBN as content, and the <<attribute-source-id-type,`@source-id-type`>> should indicate that this identifier is an ISBN.
##### Best Practice

For each source, document, and object, an identifier is specified on the corresponding attribute. If the source and document are the same, the <<attribute-source-id,`@source-id`>> attribute should be empty. If the document and object are the same, the <<attribute-object-id,`@object-id`>> attribute should be empty. The <<attribute-document-id,`@document-id`>> attribute should always be specified.

#### OPTIONAL on element:  <<element-related-object,`<related-object>`>>

|===
| Value| Meaning

| Text, numbers, or special characters| The identifier of the source for the <<element-related-object,`<related-object>`>>.
| Restriction| This is an optional attribute; there is no default.
|===
